newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU official says barley exports nearly over.
newsitem.headline: EU official says barley exports nearly over.

text.p: The European Union will not give out significant extra barley export licences this season and the 1996/97 export campaign is essentially over, an EU official said on Thursday.

The European Commission also has no intention of easing a 20 Ecu per tonne penalty on barley exports in June, nor of opening up a special round of sales from German intervention to bolster this week's barley sales to Saudi Arabia, the official said.
"The season is over, basically over" the official, who is familiar with EU export policy, told Reuters.
He did not rule out "small amounts" of extra export licences depending on the levels of bids.

He said the European Union was expected to supply 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes of the 700,000 tonnes of barley bought by Saudi Arabia on Tuesday and that this could mostly be covered by export licences already in the market.

Some market sources had speculated earlier this week that the European Union would inject new barley export licences into the market or ease loading penalties which apply in June to help exporters meet a July 15 deadline for the deliveries.
But the EU official said the Commission believed there was a healthy long position in the market and that much of the barley would be covered from other regions including Canada.
The EU has a so-called negative corrective of 20 Ecus per tonne in force for barley shipments in June, a time when southern barley from the new crop begins to surface.

The EU is a regular supplier of barley to Saudi Arabia and has seen its total barley export commitments to all destinations soar to 6.069 million tonnes from 1.559 million at a similar period last year. The season runs from July to June.
EU officials have said this is a good volume and they are happy to rest there, especially in the light of political concerns about high local grain prices, particularly for wheat.
Saudi Arabia on Tuesday bought 700,000 tonnes of feed barley to be supplied from any origin and delivered by July 15.
